goal: Build a playful, touch-first creative kiosk where visitors create and finish a layered digital paper card.
experiencePrinciples: Keep the interface direct, playful, and understandable without hidden keyboard shortcuts.
Use the existing liquid-glass shader consistently for controls and panels.
Commit buttons on pointer release; dragging outside cancels the action.
Treat touch as a primary input and prevent accidental taps from becoming paths.
Prefer simple local variables and direct calls until an abstraction removes real complexity.

architecture.runtime: Browser globals with p5.js 1.11.13, p5.sound, WebGL, and GLSL
architecture.state: scene, data, and inout globals in js/common_custom.js

importantState.textLimit: 24 non-space characters and 6 words; repeated whitespace is collapsed, limiting the layer stack to 6 word layers plus the photo
importantState.persistence: Text, word paths, colors, sizes, the snapped background palette index, edit state, per-word texture-pad coordinates, photo/word Z order, and composition viewport metadata use localStorage key playspace.text.v1; the captured photo, freehand frame, and matching viewport metadata use IndexedDB database playspace-session-v1 so an unfinished composition restores and remaps into the centered card after reload or resize; successful Card Preview Finish clears both stores
importantState.wordIdentity: Paths, colors, sizes, and texture coordinates are dictionary-based using occurrence-aware word keys

implemented: The continuous p5 render target is set to 120 fps after the optimized build proved smooth on development hardware. Scanned text PNGs are loaded only when a word needs them and downsampled to a 512px render height after decode instead of retaining all 70 full-resolution images at startup. Stable per-word texture assignments and smoothed text paths are cached, with animated path processing capped at 160 representative points while drawing remains visually live

Hidden native textarea with custom glass text field and selection UI; while the expanded field is empty, a non-persistent 50%-opacity 'type your name here' prompt jumps word-by-word in the same traveling sine wave as the frame-drawing guide and disappears on the first typed character

Glass UI label graphics are cached after rendering and rebuilt only when interaction changes their visible text, displayed value, per-character animation, caret or selection gradient, marks, or dimensions; static controls reuse the cached label every frame while caret transitions continue only until settled

The artwork has a canonical 1080x1350 (4:5) artboard displayed at 80% of the largest window fit. Outside editing it is centered. During editing, the active control column's live animated width is reserved and the artboard continuously recenters within the remaining workspace, equalizing its window-edge and control-panel gaps instead of hugging the opposite edge. Done recenters it and Edit restores the handed layout. Every frame of the handedness or panel-width animation remaps photo-frame points and text paths between consecutive artboard bounds and invalidates the cached clipped-photo buffer, so the clipped photo and all text travel with the card while preserving card-relative placement; saved and cached sessions use the same alignment metadata. The background remains full-window bleed with a non-exported 10%-opacity inverse-brightness outer tint. Card Preview crops only the rounded 5%-radius artboard; drawing stays inside the card and text paths use an 8% legibility inset
Per-word path drawing and size use transparent scanned PNG letterforms without SVG edge boiling, texture masks, gloss, or torn backing; unsupported non-letter characters retain a plain-font fallback
Touch and mouse controls with smoothing, release-to-commit, and cancellation

Liquid-glass controls, UI sound engine, and responsive sizing; the 18-step color dial produces one fixed-pitch spatialized tick per visual wedge during both direct dragging and released inertia, while cadence, subtle intensity, and envelope length follow angular speed through the final snap
Asset loading progress transforms in place into the centered idle Start control; after later completed sessions Start rises back from below

The card begins at neutral 50% grey. The former background-doodle pipeline is removed. The 500px UI-scaled p5 hue dial sits behind and below the Options panel, sharing its horizontal center on the active control side while retaining its bottom-gutter vertical center and rise-in transition. It behaves like a lucky-draw wheel with drag momentum, inertial slowdown, and six-color snapping; exact RGB bypasses glass. Its IDEAFEST-inspired silhouette uses 18 irregular ten-point brush wedges, a 300-degree fan, elevated inner opening, settle-only selected-disk morph, and subtle rotating radial nudges. The live bottom sample drives the background before snapping among F79D1F, CDDD46, DBDCDA, 7BCBBB, C1BEDF, and 4D1430

The selected dial wedge's settle morph is reversible and cohesive: its broad outer geometry contracts up to 15% toward the inner anchor with stronger influence toward the cap, slightly leading but overlapping the simultaneous ten-point circle morph; reversing restores the circle into the contracted wedge while naturally relaxing its outer width and length. The cached dial texture is reused once beneath itself as a zero-black fake shadow at 20% opacity and 2 depth units behind the exact silhouette, adding no duplicate geometry generation. Its offset retains a constant 8 UI-scaled pixel magnitude while its angle eases along the shortest arc to point directly away from the cursor, treating the pointer as a lightweight moving light source

A fixed 4:5 foreground overlay is centered and scaled exactly to the artboard bounds above all visitor content and included as the frontmost Card Preview layer. One 1080x1350 vector source, assets/frame_overlay/foreground.svg, is split once at load into unchanged multicolored artwork and a white mask from its identifiable Text path. A lightweight tint eases that mask continuously between #1d1d1d and white without rebuilding the SVG or fading the colored graphics, replacing the former PNG pair. Rendering samples two pixels inside each source edge and explicitly disables strokes so transparent-edge filtering cannot introduce a dark seam. DBDCDA, 7BCBBB, and CDDD46 target dark foreground while F79D1F, C1BEDF, and 4D1430 target light foreground; during dial motion the nearest palette anchor updates the eased target

Start opens a dimmed front camera UI with a mirrored live preview and rounded frame; Take and Cancel emerge from behind the preview and reverse behind it on exit, with camera-stream cleanup when the prompt closes

Camera startup uses iPad-friendly ideal front-camera constraints with a plain-video fallback, requires a secure HTTPS context, includes playsinline and webkit-playsinline playback hints, and reports actionable permission, installed-app, missing-camera, or busy-camera errors
Successful camera capture plays assets/sound/Camera 3.m4a and flashes the screen behind the frozen rounded viewfinder

After capture, the frozen viewfinder remains open with vertically stacked Next, Retake, and Cancel controls; Retake is red and immediately runs another countdown, while only the green Next control accepts the photo before editing, removes the underlying idle Start control, and confirms through one continuous downward card sweep that hides each stationary button before it stops rendering

After accepting a photo, visitors draw a freehand frame before editing; unfinished releases preserve the path for continuation, returning within a 64px start-point radius force-closes it with a lightly jittered connector, the bottom guide jumps word-by-word in a traveling sine wave, and a review step offers green Next or red Redraw glass controls
Closed photo frames remain fully freehand: the path receives one mild smoothing pass with no template recognition, predetermined shapes, or magnetic pull

Each captured portrait is checked locally in the browser with MediaPipe Face Detector; only overlapping portions of the visitor's frame are minimally pushed outside the inner 75% of the detected face so the outer 25% may still be crossed, the correction animates without blocking drawing, and the photo clipping remains stable

The freehand frame combines a smooth organic outline with an independently seeded triadic accent snapped to a 16px grid; both follow the same underlying path with a cohesive jelly animation built from two broad traveling lobes, five restrained detail lobes, slow whole-shape breathing, and slight tangential sway, producing prominent but non-chaotic motion while the accent retains rounded joins and occasional diagonal connections
Semantic green actions use RGB (125, 150, 100), while semantic red actions use RGB (255, 100, 125), converted to equivalent HSV values for the glass UI shader
The completed frame's bounding box defines its smallest enclosing square; the captured portrait cover-fits that square without changing aspect ratio, then clips to the hand-drawn loop

Frame confirmation immediately enters text editing, focuses the hidden input, invokes the iPad keyboard, and keeps both animated frame outlines legible over the fixed grey background with a white primary stroke

A unified glass Options panel is vertically centered on the active control side and defaults to its middle XY-only state with RGB sliders hidden. It combines the CMYG texture XY field with RGB sliders and mirrors its bottom corner handle for handedness. Dragging snaps among title-only, XY-only, and fully open 1.25x states; tapping the header cycles those states. Each RGB row independently contracts near the curved clipping boundary and restores to full width over its final reveal quarter. The title aligns toward the current window side through handedness transitions. The seamless glass pass retains the XY field's 80%-white backing, concentric radius, and animated dot grid. Its four corners control InkSpray, Pastel, MixedMedia, and SprayPaint as per-character probabilities within each word: the word length is apportioned by the XY weights, assignments are deterministically shuffled, and glyphs pop between complete PNG variants without opacity blending. Missing group letters fall back randomly to the same character from any available group, including Marker and Humanize completion assets

The Instagram Stories-style layer stack is aligned immediately above Options on the same control side. Its glass backing is titled Layer, continuously matches the Options panel's current animated width, and slides through that side's window edge with 24px UI-scaled, finger-friendly inward-growing pills; unselected pills use 35% of the current inner panel width and the selected pill expands to its full inner width, so both track every Options resize. Word pills use the same CMYG interpolation as their saved texture-pad position, while the photo pill is fixed at 20% grey; selection uses stronger opacity without replacing the layer color. Added layers expand vertically beneath the title with non-overlapping spacing. Both Layer and Options headings align toward their current window side, switching between left and right alignment through the handedness transition. Frontmost remains at top, background taps collapse selection, and vertical dragging changes plain Z order. Canvas, text bar, Texture pad, and pills retain bidirectional word selection without opening the iPad keyboard

Right-handed mode is the default: balanced artboard workspace left, all editing panels right. A circular glass '<' switch begins bottom-left opposite the controls. Pressing it starts a reversible live mirror animation: Options, Layers, Wheel, switch button, artboard, photo, and text continuously cross to their opposite positions while the label changes to '>'; the reverse transition is equally smooth. The preference is persisted under localStorage key playspace.control-side.v1 only after the transition settles, preventing mid-animation cache mismatch. All side controls and the switch hide on Done while the artboard returns to center

Take Picture runs a three-second 3-2-1 countdown with matching full-opacity numerals centered in the side gutters between the viewfinder and window edges, sized to 25% of the shorter window dimension, plus rising synthesized notes; the scale is configurable as major, harmonic, or harmonicMinor in scene.session.camera.countdown.scale

Captured photos fill their visitor-drawn frame on the creative canvas and become their own sticker layer in Card Preview; Cancel, Escape, or a background tap returns to editing without clearing, while successful Finish ends the session and returns to idle Start

A new session starts empty with one randomly selected exact color from the six-color background palette, excluding the immediately previous session color so a fresh assignment is always visible, unless an unfinished localStorage and IndexedDB session is restored after refresh; the photo, frame, text, size, colors, and texture coordinates survive reload, while successful digital-card confirmation is the finish boundary

Centered perspective Card Preview enters from below with a smooth one-turn presentation spin and remains draggable with inertial orbit at 25% viewport scale. Once inertia slows, the card eases to whichever of two resting states is nearest: upright front or upright back; a new drag immediately interrupts the snap. The fixed grey background forms the digital-paper base; the framed photo and every ordered word are captured as transparent sticker planes distributed evenly across 28 WebGL depth units, producing 4-unit gaps for seven layers. Photo and text stickers receive 55/255-alpha soft silhouette shadows projected onto the card surface with only a 0.01-unit anti-flicker offset, while the foreground overlay remains shadow-free; a separate blended shadow pass temporarily disables depth writes so equal-depth shadows remain visible together before the raised stickers render normally. Rotation reveals the resulting parallax while the 2% white frame, preview-only Humanize PlaySpace back mark, WebGL lighting, animated glass controls, and dimmed main UI remain
During editing, Finish slides offscreen and is inactive while the text field expands left; Done collapses the field into Edit and returns Finish
Developer alignment guides toggle with Shift+/ (?) and follow the pointer with red horizontal and vertical lines
nextPriorities: Design a start-to-finish public kiosk session with reset and inactivity timeout
Validate the layered digital-card finish and memory use on iPadOS
Continue performance profiling on tablet hardware as assets and effects increase
continuationInstructions: Work from the repository root, then modify only creators/louism/PlaySpace unless explicitly requested otherwise.
Run git status and inspect existing diffs before editing; never discard uncommitted user work.
Keep the current global p5 architecture unless a requested change clearly justifies refactoring.
Test visual changes at desktop, iPad portrait, and a narrow mobile viewport.
Do not commit or push until the user requests it.

development.notes: There are no automated tests or npm scripts. Validate rendering, console output, touch/mouse interaction, audio startup, Loading-to-Start, camera permission/live capture/cancel, editing, and the perspective Card Preview manually.

worktreeAtLastUpdate.status: Uncommitted local changes include the Loading-to-Start session flow, camera capture, and print-preview implementation. Inspect git diff for the authoritative current state.
